question: Why did North America bring in so much more completed revenue than LATAM in 2024?

sql_attempts.sql: SELECT r.region_name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS customer_count, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)), 2) AS revenue, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)) / COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id), 2) AS average_order_value FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN regions AS r ON c.region_id = r.region_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.order_date BETWEEN '2024-01-01' AND '2024-12-31' AND r.region_name IN ('North America', 'LATAM') GROUP BY r.region_name LIMIT 500

answer: North America generated significantly higher completed revenue in 2024 ($3,964,289.71) than LATAM ($1,282,093.87) primarily due to a much higher order volume (1,229 orders vs. 434) and a larger customer base (361 customers vs. 128). Furthermore, North America sold more total units (9,438 vs. 3,196) and maintained a higher average order value ($3,225.62 vs. $2,954.13).
